question.problem:
By changing the order of integration in the following double integrals, express the following sum as a single double integral.

$$
{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{1}^{3}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y+{\int }_{1}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡3+1}{\int }_{{e}^{y-1}}^{3}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y
$$
question.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14225558/assets/314b881b95ea804456b3e41a1d8fec70cf459e007e2120d9018e3bef02f1b523.png)

The diagram above shows the region of integration. It consists of two type II regions, given by

$$
\begin{aligned}D & =\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le y\le 1,\,1\le x\le 3\}\,\cup \,\{(x,y)\,:\,1\le y\le \operatorname{ln}⁡3+1,\,{e}^{y-1}\le x\le 3\}.\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that the top boundary of the region, written in the form $x=x(y),$ is

$$
x={e}^{y-1}\,⟹\,y=\operatorname{ln}⁡x+1,
$$

and the bottom boundary of the region is

$$
y=0.
$$

To change the order of integration, we write $D$ as a type I region. The type I representation of the region is

$$
D=\{(x,y)\,:\,1\le x\le 3,\,0\le y\le \operatorname{ln}⁡x+1\},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14225558/assets/c9b097164e2b5215a051e18de055f3cce4c26600caf510bc3b0071b77b645089.png)

Therefore, swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{1}^{3}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y+{\int }_{1}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡3+1}{\int }_{{e}^{y-1}}^{3}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y & ={\int }_{1}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡x+1}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$
